intro: A finding is an actively exploited vulnerability (CISA KEV, or VulnCheck KEV if you turned it on) that matches one of your devices. Confirmed means a safe scan template saw the vulnerability; suspected means it only matches by version or product.
caption: Findings list

versionNeeded.title_one: Add the version of 1 software to check it
versionNeeded.title_other: Add the version of {{count}} software to check them
versionNeeded.help: Vedette compares the version with the versions each exploited CVE affects. Without a version it cannot tell, so it lists the product here once instead of one finding per CVE. Open the device and add the version.
versionNeeded.missing_one: <sw>{{software}}</sw> has no version: adding it checks 1 exploited CVE.
versionNeeded.missing_other: <sw>{{software}}</sw> has no version: adding it checks {{count}} exploited CVEs.
versionNeeded.unreadable_one: <sw>{{software}}</sw> version "{{version}}" cannot be compared: enter it as numbers (for example 7.2.5) to check 1 exploited CVE.
versionNeeded.unreadable_other: <sw>{{software}}</sw> version "{{version}}" cannot be compared: enter it as numbers (for example 7.2.5) to check {{count}} exploited CVEs.

emptyCve: No findings for {{cve}} in this filter.
emptyHelp: Vedette only matches vulnerabilities against devices it knows. If you have no devices yet, add them first; once you do, run a scan to check right away. Vedette will tell you when a new vulnerability matches.

headline.confirmed: {{device}} has a confirmed vulnerability ({{cve}}) that is being exploited in the wild
headline.suspected: {{device}} may be affected by {{cve}}: needs checking
headline.mitigated: {{device}}: {{cve}} is mitigated, patching is still needed to remove it

device.title: Findings on this device
device.description: Exploited vulnerabilities that match this device.
device.none: No findings for this device yet.
device.handleAll: Select and handle these findings in the Findings list

status.title: Mark as handled
status.description: Record a new status for {{cve}}. History is kept so others know who changed it and why.
status.noteRequired: Say why this is a false positive or not relevant (at least 3 characters).
status.patchedHint: The vendor patch is installed. Rescan to confirm.
status.mitigatedHint: Not patched, but the way in is blocked (for example Internet access cut off).
status.false_positiveHint: The device is not affected; Vedette matched it wrongly.
status.not_relevantHint: Affected, but no action needed (for example a device being retired, not on the network).
status.accept_riskHint: Known and not fixed yet, for a reason (for example no patch window before March). The finding reopens by itself after the date.

evidence.title: Evidence
evidence.description: Why Vedette thinks this device is affected, and how you can check it yourself.
evidence.none: No scan evidence for this finding yet.
evidence.noTemplate: No safe scan template for this CVE yet
evidence.noTemplateRun: A template exists; not yet run on this device
evidence.recheckCode: Run from a machine on the internal network
evidence.noIpScan: This device has no IP address in your inventory, so Vedette cannot scan it. Add its IP on the device page to scan it.

rec.title: What to do
rec.description: The source of a recommendation is always stated: confirmed by Vedette maintainers, or none yet.
rec.appliedHint: Only writes a log entry. The finding changes status after you mark it or rescan.
rec.confirmedBy: Confirmed by {{by}} on {{date}} through a GitHub pull request. Drafted with AI, every step checked by a maintainer.
rec.workaroundTitle: 2. Temporary workaround if you cannot update yet
rec.firewallTitle: 3. Firewall configuration to cut off access
rec.firewallHint: Each command is in its own box; paste them one at a time, in order. Read the side effects before pasting.
rec.fwDetected: Pre-selected the firewall vendor you declared in the inventory.
rec.fwNone: You have not declared a firewall in the inventory, so below is general guidance and reference syntax.
rec.checklistHint: Tick as you finish ({{done}}/{{total}}). Only for tracking on this screen; not saved.
rec.noPackBody: Vedette maintainers have not confirmed a step-by-step pack for this CVE yet. Below is everything this box knows: what the exploited list requires, where the vendor's fix is, and how to check your device. It is source information, not a Vedette recommendation. Your own AI can draft more; its answer always carries the AI-generated label.
rec.sourceHint: CISA's required action when it added this vulnerability on {{date}} (original English).
rec.sourceHintVulnCheck: VulnCheck KEV's note when it added this vulnerability on {{date}} (original English). CISA does not list it yet.
rec.dueDate: CISA's deadline for US federal agencies: {{date}}. Use it as your own deadline.
rec.ransomware: Ransomware groups have used this flaw, so handle it before the deadline.
rec.noFixedVersion: Vedette does not have the fixed version for this CVE yet. The vendor advisory says which version fixes it.
rec.fixedIn: Fixed in {{fixed}}: upgrade {{device}} from {{version}} to {{fixed}} or later.
rec.fixedFeatureUpdate: NVD names the fix for {{branch}} ({{fixed}}), not for the Windows release {{device}} runs ({{version}}): Microsoft no longer updates that release, so no monthly update brings it this fix. Move {{device}} to a Windows release Microsoft still services (a feature update). If Windows Update still offers it monthly updates, install the latest and check Microsoft's advisory.
rec.fixedEsu: Fixed in {{fixed}}, an Extended Security Update: Microsoft updates {{branch}} past the end of its support only for devices enrolled in Extended Security Updates. If {{device}} (now {{version}}) is enrolled, install it; otherwise move {{device}} to a Windows release Microsoft still services.
rec.fixedUpTo: Versions up to {{fixed}} are affected, and {{device}} runs {{version}}: upgrade to a release after {{fixed}}. The version data does not name it; the vendor advisory does.
rec.fixedBranches: {{device}} has no version yet, so Vedette lists the fix of each release line: {{list}}. Add the version to see the one for this device.
rec.fixedUnreadable: Vedette cannot read the version "{{version}}" of {{device}}, so it lists the fix of each release line: {{list}}. Correct the version on the Devices page to see the one for this device.
rec.fixedDistro: {{device}} runs {{product}} {{version}} from {{distro}}'s packages, in the affected range: install {{distro}}'s security updates for it (for example apt upgrade) and check {{distro}}'s notice for this CVE.
rec.fixedDistroAny: {{device}} runs {{product}} {{version}} from its distribution's packages, in the affected range: install the distribution's security updates for it (for example apt upgrade or dnf upgrade) and check its notice for this CVE.
rec.fixedDistroBelow: {{distro}} backports fixes, so the package's version number may stay below {{fixed}}, the upstream release that fixes it.
rec.fixedDistroBelowAny: The distribution backports fixes, so the package's version number may stay below {{fixed}}, the upstream release that fixes it.
rec.fixedIfDistro: If you installed {{product}} from {{distro}}'s packages, install its security updates instead (for example apt upgrade): {{distro}} backports the fix under its own version number, so the number above may never appear.
rec.fixedNoFix: no fixed release named for {{count}} more line(s)
rec.fixedSource: Source: {{source}}. Check the vendor advisory before you upgrade.
rec.fixedDistroIn: Fixed in {{fixed}} for {{distro}} {{release}}: {{device}} has {{product}} {{version}} from {{distro}}'s packages. Install {{distro}}'s security updates for it (for example apt upgrade).
rec.fixedDistroPro: This fix is in Ubuntu Pro (ESM) only: the machine needs an Ubuntu Pro subscription to receive it.
rec.noVendorLink: The exploited list gives no vendor link for this flaw. Search the vendor's security advisories for {{cve}} ({{product}}).
rec.step1: Find which version of {{product}} {{device}} runs, and add it to the device on the Devices page so Vedette can compare it.
rec.step2Due: If it is older than the fixed version in the advisory, update it by {{date}}.
rec.step2: If it is older than the fixed version in the advisory, update it.
rec.step3: Then press "I updated" at the top of this page and type the new version: Vedette checks it and closes every finding on {{device}} that version fixes. For software a scan reads, run a scan of {{device}} instead.
rec.step3Mark: Then mark this finding as Patched. If the version is already fixed, mark it as False positive and write the version in the note.
rec.noKev: This CVE is not on an exploited list this box holds (the list may have dropped it, or VulnCheck KEV was turned off), so there is no source information to show.

compromise.title: Have I been hit?
compromise.description: Signs that the device was exploited, and commands to check yourself.
compromise.none: No confirmed exploitation signs for this CVE yet. Follow the recheck steps under Evidence and look at the device logs around the day the vulnerability was published.

explain.description: Your AI explains whether this device is affected and why.

ai.unavailable: The AI assistant is off, or no AI profile is assigned to this job.

risk.unverifiedHint: Unverified: product match only. Vedette knows the product but not its version, so this may not apply to you. Add the version on the device page, or run a scan, to check.
risk.unverifiedLine: Unverified: product match only. The severity applies only if the version on this device is affected.

bulk.tooMany: At most {{max}} at a time. Narrow the filter.
bulk.description: One status and one note for every selected open finding. Findings already closed keep their status and note. Each finding keeps its own history line, so others can see who changed it and why.
bulk.noteHint: The same note is saved on each finding.
bulk.skipped_one: {{count}} was already closed and kept its status.
bulk.skipped_other: {{count}} were already closed and kept their status.

accept.untilHint: From tomorrow up to one year.
accept.noteRequired: Say why you accept the risk (at least 3 characters).
accept.untilRequired: Choose a date from tomorrow up to one year from today.

updated.title: I updated {{software}}
updated.description: Type the version {{device}} runs now. Vedette checks every finding of {{software}} against it: the ones this version fixes close by themselves, the others stay open.
updated.noCurrent: Vedette has no version for it yet.
updated.required: Type the version it runs now, for example 7.4.5.
updated.same: Vedette already has {{version}}. Type the version it runs after the update.
updated.bad_version: "{{version}}" is not a version Vedette can store: use letters, digits, dots, hyphens and brackets, up to 40 characters, for example 7.4.5.
updated.duplicate_software: {{software}} {{version}} is already on {{device}}. Remove the older {{software}} on the device page instead.
updated.not_manual: Vedette reads this version from the device. Run a scan of {{device}} to check.
updated.closed_one: 1 finding on {{device}} no longer applies and was closed.
updated.closed_other: {{count}} findings on {{device}} no longer apply and were closed.
updated.pending: Vedette is checking the new version; this list updates in a moment.
updated.scanned: Vedette reads this version from the device. Run a scan of {{device}} to check.
updated.agent: The agent on {{device}} reports the new version by itself, usually within two hours after the restart that finishes the update. The findings the update fixes then close by themselves.

closed.mitigated: Closed as mitigated{{who}}{{when}}. Patching is still needed to remove it
closed.systemNotRelevant: Vedette closed this as not relevant{{when}}
closed.risk_accepted: Risk accepted until {{date}}{{who}}{{when}}. It reopens by itself after that day
